literature.title: Mode of action of tubulozoles against Plasmodium falciparum in vitro.
literature.abstract: The mode of action of the tubulozole isomers, recently recognized as a new class of potential antimalarial agents, was investigated. Whereas neither glycolysis, protease activity, or nucleic acid biosynthesis was primarily affected, protein biosynthesis decreased soon after addition of the drug. Inhibitors of protein biosynthesis, however, did not show synergistic activity with tubulozole. Colcemid, on the other hand, had an effect on protein synthesis similar to that seen with the tubulozoles.

literature.title: Compounds binding to cytoskeletal proteins are active against Plasmodium falciparum in vitro.
literature.abstract: The effects of nine different tubulin-binding substances and of one actin-binding compound, cytochalasin B, upon the intraerythrocytic development of the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum were investigated in vitro. From the data obtained, plasmodial tubulins seem to be quite different from the mammalian proteins on the molecular level. Tubulozole-T, a substance which is inactive in mammalian systems, appears to be a promising novel antimalarial drug.

literature.abstract: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disorder predominantly affecting individuals of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern descent, including those with certain heritages including Sephardic Jewish, Armenian, Turkish, and Arab. The disorder affects up to 1 in 200 people making it a very common etiology for pain states worldwide, including serositis mediated painful states of the chest, joint, and abdomen.

literature.title: Arterial stiffness in Familial Mediterranean Fever: correlations with disease-related parameters and colchicine treatment.
literature.abstract: Familial Mediterranean Fever is the most common autoinflammatory disease. As chronic inflammation may result in increased arterial stiffness, we aimed to investigate indices of arterial stiffness in patients with Familial Mediterranean Fever and their associations with disease-related factors and colchicine treatment.

repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: Colchicine 抑制微管聚合 → 阻斷嗜中性球趨化 → 抑制 NLRP3 inflammasome 激活 → 降低 IL-1β/IL-18 驅動的週期性發炎。FMF 病理核心 (MEFV 突變 → pyrin 失調) 正是此路徑的靶標，為國際第一線標準治療。
DFSP 由 COL1A1-PDGFB 融合基因驅動 PDGFR 持續活化；colchicine 的抗微管機制可能抑制腫瘤細胞分裂，但無選擇性靶向 DFSP 的直接依據。TxGNN 預測可能源自炎症/增生通路的圖譜相似性。

repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: Colchicine 調節先天免疫（嗜中性球、炎症小體），理論上可能緩解部分先天免疫失調；但原發性免疫缺乏的遺傳缺陷種類繁多（>430 種），colchicine 的抗炎機制對以免疫缺乏（而非過度活化）為特徵的病況可能無益甚至有害。
Sitosterolemia 由 ABCG5/ABCG8 突變導致植物固醇累積；colchicine 對脂質轉運無直接作用。TxGNN 預測可能源自 colchicine 對心血管炎症的已知保護效果（間接關聯），而非對此罕見病的特異性機轉。
Colchicine 可能抑制肥大細胞脫顆粒（體外數據），但 smouldering SM 的 KIT D816V 驅動的肥大細胞增生需靶向 KIT 抑制劑（midostaurin, avapritinib）。colchicine 缺乏對此亞型的特異性機轉支持。

literature.title: Histamine elevation in familial Mediterranean fever: A study from the Juvenile Inflammatory Rheumatism cohort.
literature.abstract: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) is the most frequent monogenic autoinflammatory disease (AID). Some patients have persistent symptoms despite colchicine intake. Mast cells (MC) are innate immune cells involved in inflammatory conditions including AID. Their activation is responsible for various symptoms such as abdominal pain, bloating and pruritus.

此罕見亞型（SM-AHN 中的嗜酸性球變異）由 KIT 突變與 FIP1L1-PDGFRA 融合驅動；colchicine 無靶向 PDGFRA 或 KIT 的依據。
